title: Middle-earth Is Back: 'The Rings of Power' Season 3 Drops Four Episodes Today — and the One Ring Is Finally Forged
excerpt: After more than two years away, 'The Rings of Power' returns to Prime Video today with four episodes at once — five years after Eregion fell, with Sauron building Barad-dûr.
content:
After a wait of more than two years, Middle-earth is back. The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power returns to Prime Video today, Wednesday, November 11, with the first four episodes of Season 3 dropping at once, at 3 a.m. ET / midnight PT.

The new season picks up five years after the fall of Eregion, with Sauron — played by Charlie Vickers — beginning work on Barad-dûr and the war between the Elves and the Dark Lord at its height. The Season 2 finale aired October 3, 2024, so the return comes more than two years after the story last left off, with the Elven realms regrouping and Númenor under the rule of Ar-Pharazûn.

Season 3 runs eight episodes in total: four today, two more on November 18, and the final two on November 25. The whole season lands in three weeks, streaming in more than 240 countries and territories.

This is the season the series has been building toward from the start: the forging of the One Ring. At the end of Season 2, nineteen Rings of Power existed — the Three for the Elves, the Seven for the Dwarves, the Nine for Men — but the One Ring had not yet been made. Season 3 is the one that finally brings it to the screen.

The returning cast includes Morfydd Clark as Galadriel, Robert Aramayo as Elrond, Cynthia Addai-Robinson as Queen Regent Míriel and Vickers as Sauron. The new faces include Jamie Campbell Bower as Celeborn, Galadriel’s long-lost husband, Eddie Marsan as Thrain, Zubin Varla as Khamûl, Andrew Richardson as Anarion, and Adam Young as Marnükh, with Simon Pegg voicing the Balrog.

Early word is split, as it has been for the series from the start. Season 2 holds an 85% Tomatometer from 173 reviews against a 58% audience score on Rotten Tomatoes, as of November 10. Decider’s Season 3 review says the show is “finally truly epic,” while other critics are divided on Sauron’s big war.

The binge-style rollout is deliberate. Co-showrunner Patrick McKay told io9 the creators feel the show “plays better on a binge because it really is so highly serialized,” and wanted viewers to be able to watch it over the holidays.

Analysis: The moment the whole series was building toward

Two years is a long time to keep an audience waiting, and Amazon knows it — four episodes at once is a statement that the wait is over and the story is ready to be devoured, not rationed. The forging of the One Ring is the hinge the entire series turns on: everything from the first season’s mystery-box plotting to the fall of Eregion was groundwork for this. If the divided audience comes back, it will be because this season finally delivers the event Tolkien fans have been waiting for since the show was announced. If it does not, the three-week sprint to the finale will at least settle the argument fast.
